newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF official says quotas to dominate Sept meeting.
newsitem.headline: IMF official says quotas to dominate Sept meeting.

text.p: Quota increases and liberalisation of capital accounts will dominate the International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual meeting in September in Hong Kong, Hubert Neiss, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department said on Friday.
"The main issue is the quota increase and the growing interest in the IMF in capital account liberalisation. These are the two issues," Neiss told Reuters.
The joint IMF/World Bank annual meeting will be the first major international extravaganza to be held in Hong Kong after the British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30 1997.

Hard hit by huge loans to Mexico and Russia in recent years, the IMF needs to replenish coffers through a massive increase in quotas. IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said earlier that the quota increases will need to be "substantial."
Said Neiss: "This will be an increase for everybody, all the membership is involved."
Camdessus is believed to want quotas to double to a total of US$440 billion, reports from Washington say.
